title: Voice Activity Detection & Turn-Taking — Silero, Cobra, and the Flush Trick
service: TurnKit: an energy gate, a SQLite table of sample-exact speech segments, a turn-end state machine with pre-roll and flush, a streaming gate-then-model VAD cascade, and the overlap structure of a conversation

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It, Step 1: the energy gate (RMS, dBFS, -40 dBFS threshold); Tier 1 of the cascade
planted_bugs: rms returns the signed mean of the samples; the negative 'level' surfaces one call later as ValueError: math domain error in dbfs, whose guard only covers digital silence
energy_gate compares the mean square (a power) with the threshold converted to an amplitude, 10 ** (dB / 20), so frames between -40 and -20 dBFS read as silence
energy_gate converts hangover_ms into frames by dividing by frame_len (samples) instead of frame_ms, so the hangover is 0 frames at 8 and 16 kHz
apply_hangover looks for the last loud frame by scanning the whole history for every frame, O(n^2)
parts.timing_assert: apply_hangover on 16,000 frames (about five minutes of 20 ms frames: 20 s of talk, then a long quiet stretch) under 0.1 s; the quadratic version takes about 1.3 s (1.33-1.44 s measured), a backward scan that stops at the first loud frame about 1.1 s (1.09-1.21 s), the fixed one about 0.4 ms
parts.overfix_guard: the usual O(n) rewrites break the edges: a 'frames since the last loud frame' counter that starts at 0 marks the leading silence as speech, and the window slice loud[i - frames : i + 1] goes negative at the start and loses a loud first frame

parts.lesson_anchor: Step 2 get_speech_timestamps returns sample offsets; skill-vad-tuner guard 'audit log every VAD-fire event for tuning'

deviations: Part 1 keeps to measurement and the frame-level hangover. The suggested guard 'a single loud frame must not start speech' (minimum speech duration) moves to Part 3, where the lesson puts min_speech_ms; Part 1's guards are the two edges the usual O(n) rewrite of the hangover gets wrong.
Part 1's dBFS/linear mix-up is a power (mean square) compared with an amplitude threshold, not a wrong dBFS formula, so it does not repeat a dBFS-meter bug; dbfs itself is correct as shipped.

Part 3 has no maximum turn length: the lesson never mentions one. Its place is taken by pre-roll (a Key parameter and a Pitfall, unused in the lesson's code) and by flush, the detector's side of the lesson's flush trick; the service shows the STT side (audio, then flush, as soon as a turn ends).
Part 4 stops at Tiers 1 and 2. Tier 3 is Part 3's detector, so the cascade's correctness is checked on frame decisions, model calls and the model's context instead of on turns.
Part 4 uses server-sent events rather than NDJSON, which 06/03 already uses.

Part 5: the lesson has no tree of its own. The overlap structure of a conversation (turns, backchannels inside them, talk-over nested to any depth) is the nested structure turn-taking produces, and it is built from flat per-speaker segments like the ones Part 2 stores.
